notes: The direction is settled and this does not reopen it. A crossing rate is applied when the generator draws a name for a gender it already holds; no name is ever read to infer a gender.
A band per direction is more useful than a figure. A rate the game can defend as roughly right is actionable; a decimal would read as a measurement the game never made.

The neutral pool is thirty-six names sorted by hand and is currently reachable only by people recorded non-binary. Whether those names belong to everyone at some rate is part of the same question, not a separate one. GIVEN_NAME_GENERATION_POOLS_V1 says so itself at names-data.ts:1158 — it is an authored partition, not a field lifted from the source, so there is no measured crossing rate anywhere in the tree.

MEASURED CROSSING EXISTS, BUT NOT A RATE. Against the SSA decade data now in hand (docs/research/evidence/ssa-given-names-by-decade.json on claude/project-thread-k8w14s at a4f30ed0 — do not commission it again), five names appear on both the male and the female top 100 OF THE SAME DECADE: Willie in the 1920s, Terry in the 1950s, Jamie in the 1970s, Jordan in the 1990s and 2000s, Taylor in the 1990s. Two top-100 appearances prove a name was carried by both sexes in that decade. They say nothing about what share of people named Jordan were girls, which is the rate this question asks for, and that needs the per-name-per-year count files whose download the network policy refuses. The five names must not be read as an answer.

THE FINDING THOSE FIVE CARRY IS A SCHEMA CONSEQUENCE, not only a content one. Each crossing is tied to its decade: a shared name is something a generation does rather than a standing property of the name. The thirty-six-name neutral pool carries no era on any entry, so the current data model CANNOT EXPRESS that finding even once the rate is known. An answer that hands back a single national band is an answer the shape cannot hold. See [given-name-fashion-by-birth-year], which is the same evidence read from the other end.

DOC84 clause 3 (Drive 1Qg4zfzf8Nz8w8OuD3LUjz9JCqnv842totI29fsaxJTM, 2026-08-28) specifies SSA national and state baby-name frequency files "for cohort-aware given names" plus Census surnames, and forbids inferring race or ethnicity from a surname. That constraint binds any answer here.
This is a generation rule, never an observation: it must never be read back as a claim about any particular person, real or generated.
question: In the United States, how often is a given name that most people read as belonging to one gender actually carried by someone of another gender, and how does that rate vary — by the name itself, by the decade somebody was born in, and by whether the name is a long-established one or a recent arrival? Which names are genuinely shared rather than read one way with exceptions?
requestedBy: gendered given names thread (technical team lead)

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Carries the partition in use — 171 male, 139 female, 36 neutral, covering all 346 corpus names exactly once — and nothing recorded says how the three were sorted, on what evidence, or how often the sorting should be crossed. The header states the corpus deliberately carries no demographic attribute, so the partition sits beside the corpus rather than in it.

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Shows the draw: a stated or generated gender selects one of three pools and the name comes from inside it, with no crossing at all. The place a rate would be applied is one function; the rate itself is not recorded anywhere.

sourcesChecked.source: U.S. Social Security Administration National Data on the Relative Frequency of Given Names, cited as the corpus provenance in names-data.ts
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: The published tables report counts by sex per name per year, which is exactly the shape an answer needs, but the repository holds only the curated name list drawn from them and not the counts. Nothing here has read the underlying frequencies, and the egress proxy blocks the publisher.

Settles the direction — gender is the input to name generation and a name is never read backwards to decide a gender — which this question does not disturb. It says nothing about how tightly the input should constrain the draw.

title: How often an American given name is carried by someone of another gender
usableAnswer: A crossing rate the generator can apply, expressed as a band rather than a figure: roughly what share of people carrying a name read as male are not male, and the same the other way, with the reasoning behind it. A line on whether that share moves with birth decade and in which direction. A list of the given names that are genuinely shared in American use rather than read one way with exceptions, so the neutral pool can be drawn from real usage rather than from a hand-sorted list. If the honest answer is that the rate is too name-specific to give as one band, say so and say what the generator should key on instead.
whyItMatters: THIS IS A BLOCKER ON A LIVE REGRESSION, not an improvement. The generator draws a given name from the pool that matches the gender the world recorded, which is what stops a man being named Maria. Drawn strictly, it can never produce a woman called Michael or a man called Ashley, and those people exist. That is already shipped: a player who selects Female and leaves the name blank goes through statedGenderGivenName in people.ts:583 and cannot be given Jordan, today, on main. And it is total rather than merely unlikely: Jordan sits in the 36-name NEUTRAL pool, which that function reaches only when the player is recorded non-binary, so a stated-female draw takes the 139-name female pool and Jordan is unreachable by any path at all — not at a low rate, never. The same holds for every name the hand-authored partition filed as neutral. The repair to generated people widens it from the player and six household roles to every person the world invents. So the draw is now strictly incapable of something real, behind a placeholder partition nobody can see, which is the exact shape this project keeps rediscovering months later and calling never started. The rate was not invented in its place because a national constant standing in for something that varies by name and by birth decade is its own defect; that decision is deliberate and it is what this question unblocks. A partition with no crossing rate is a national constant standing in for something that varies by name and by generation, which is the same defect in the other direction: believable at every single person and wrong across a population. The game already has the birth year of every person it generates, so a rate that moves by decade is usable rather than decorative.

answer.summary:
A single crossing percentage is not supported. Use the source's per-name, birth-year and recorded-sex counts as the factual naming evidence; a name may occur in multiple categories with different frequencies. Names shared across categories are not reserved for nonbinary characters. Never infer a person's gender from their generated or chosen name.

SSA records sex on applications, not a present-day gender-identity distribution; errors and naming changes mean rare cross-category entries cannot be equated automatically to transgender/nonbinary prevalence. Character identity stays an independently recorded input. Any mapping from historical naming evidence to current generated identity is an explicitly authored, editable game rule, with player-name override preserved. Do not call it a measured identity rate.

Suppressed counts below five are not observed zeros. Keep the published record's scope: national files exclude territory births, which have separate products. This batch answers the method, not a compiled numeric table; the data owner should receive actual source counts through the established data path before claiming factual frequency weights.

Acceptance ChatGPT requests (not executed): A genuinely shared name can be generated for more than one applicable identity; no name read-back changes gender. A suppressed cell is not treated as proven impossibility. Current named characters are not renamed after an importer update.
